A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GAF, with matching authors, core pipeline and datasets. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original avatar-reconstruction experiments, quantitative baseline comparisons, ablations, frame-count robustness results and qualitative reenactments.

after.justification: V2 retains original reconstruction experiments and adds baseline results, direct diffusion-conditioning comparisons and a 3D-aware-denoising ablation.

M1.justification: The proposed Gaussian-avatar representation, normal-map-conditioned multi-view diffusion, iterative pseudo-ground-truth supervision, latent upsampling and optimization losses are retained. V2 identifies the upsampler as pretrained and adds experimental controls without establishing a change to the proposed architecture or core algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use NeRSemble and the INSTA/smartphone Monocular Video data for head reconstruction, novel views, expressions and reenactment. Diffusion-generated novel views already appear in v1 Appendix C; v2's additional conditioning tests do not introduce a new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PanoHead, SphereHead, P4D-v2 and GAGAvatar to the existing INSTA, FlashAvatar and GaussianAvatars comparisons. P4D-v2 and GAGAvatar also enter Table 2. The static PanoHead and SphereHead models are evaluated only for novel views, substantially broadening the comparator families.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 replaces viewpoint sampling specified by azimuth, elevation and distance ranges with sampling four of fifteen NeRSemble viewpoints. The rendering-speed benchmark changes resolution from 768×768 to 802×550, and new ablations introduce additional controls. Existing dataset splits and optimization budgets remain unchanged; the reported setting revision does not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds ray-map conditioning to the reconstruction ablations, directly evaluates pose-, ray-map- and normal-map-conditioned diffusion using metrics and error maps, and tests removal of 3D-aware denoising in Appendix B.4/Table 7. These substantially extend the mechanism checks. The earlier frame-count robustness and reenactment analyses are retained, with robustness relocated to the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report sequence averages and point estimates without experimental seed specifications, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes GAF's novel-view LPIPS/PSNR/SSIM from 0.158/19.20/87.00 to 0.125/20.88/88.91 and updates its expression scores. Added GAGAvatar results place it above GAF in novel-view PSNR, 21.20 versus 20.88. Table 2 changes GAF's L1/PSNR/SSIM from 0.0228/23.01/89.93 to 0.0229/23.16/89.76. V2 also adds conditioning and denoising results and revises rendering speed from 384.3 to 62 FPS. Changed viewpoint sampling and rendering resolution preclude treating these updates as controlled cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The Gaussian transformations, conditional-distribution formulation and optimization equations remain unchanged. Position and scale regularization equations 7–8 move from Section 4.3 to Appendix B.3. V2 condenses the explanatory SDS discussion without adding or substantively revising theoretical assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 removes the specific 5.34% SSIM improvement headline from the abstract and introduction. The introduction instead emphasizes performance across novel views and expressions on NeRSemble and commodity videos, while the conclusion explicitly identifies the upsampler as pretrained. The central methodological contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of the new baselines' failures, including GAGAvatar identity drift and limited expression/detail recovery by feed-forward methods. It also explicitly argues that novel-view constraints benefit novel-expression synthesis and extends the alignment discussion to ray-map conditioning. The stated relighting, optimization-time and hair-modeling limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.4 discloses ablation implementation details, including SH=0 for the no-diffusion GaussianAvatars variant and DreamBooth fine-tuning of the U-Net and text encoder for 500 iterations at a learning rate of 5e-6. V2 also identifies and references the pretrained Stable Diffusion x2 latent upscaler. These are documentation additions rather than evidence that retained ablations changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of feed-forward avatars including P4D, P4D-v2, GAGAvatar and MGGTalk, and broadens its diffusion-based 3D-generation references. PanoHead and SphereHead also enter the comparison context. The central positioning around head-specific, normal-map-conditioned multi-view priors remains intact; the revised VHAP reference denotes the same work.

P1.justification: V2 locally revises the abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion, and shortens the SDS explanation. Regularization details move to Appendix B.3, frame-count robustness moves to Appendix D.4, and Appendix B.4 organizes ablation implementations. The overall narrative and main section structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The comparison displays are substantially revised: Figures 4 and 11 expand from six to ten columns, Figure 5 changes displayed comparators, and Figure 6 adds ray-map conditioning. V2 introduces conditioning predictions/error maps and two analysis tables, adds ranking highlights to Table 1, and relocates the robustness plots and several appendix figures.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical support through broader prior-based and feed-forward baseline comparisons and additional mechanism tests. Ablation implementation details and explicit upscaler attribution improve reproducibility and credit, while the results discussion acknowledges GAGAvatar's PSNR lead. These provide a supported overall quality gain, although changed viewpoint sampling limits what can be inferred from the revised headline scores.
